Part 1

What does a PFD add to the block flow diagram, and how is this sheet read?

Part 1 · the plan

From eight blocks to one engineering sheet

  1. What the PFD addsequipment, numbered streams, process valves, operating data
  2. The sheet, layer by layerwhat each kind of mark on RF-CAS-v1-PFD-001 carries
  3. SymbolsISO 10628 shapes and where each one sits
  4. Stream numbers and flagsPFD numbers against Process-tab numbers; one flag read in full

BFD versus PFD

Four things the PFD adds to the block diagram

The BFD says what each block does; the PFD shows how.

Equipment

13 items, symbol and tag; the BFD has eight blocks.

Streams

25 numbered, including those inside a BFD block.

Valves

Only the ones that define the process.

Operating data

Flow, temperature, pressure flags; utilities.

Isolation valves, drains, vents and relief devices are left for the P&ID.

The sheet, layer by layer

Each layer answers one question — what, where it flows, what controls it, and at what conditions.

ISO 10628 symbols, found on the sheet

The shape says what the item does — three exchangers carry process fluid on both sides.

Interactive — click a stream number

PFD numbers and Process-tab numbers

Four PFD streams have no Process number — the PFD shows flows the BFD keeps inside a block.

Reading the marks

One information flag, one equipment tag

Tag partMeaning
E · V · Kexchanger · vessel · compressor
1xxgas train
2xxpropylene loop
3xxethylene loop

E-203 carries a 2: propylene boils in its shell, ethylene condenses in its tubes.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The PFD adds equipment, numbered streams, process valves and data.
  • Each layer of the sheet answers one question.
  • 25 PFD streams map onto the Process-tab streams; four have no match.
  • A flag reads mass flow, temperature, pressure, top to bottom.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Thirteen items; every duty ends in the cooling water of E-201 or E-301.
  • Feed 42.17 t/h leaves as two liquids and the off-gas.
  • Each loop balances: heat in equals heat out.
  • 41 of 41 flag values agree with the model’s design point.

Reading the PFD for operation

Five rules for reading this sheet

Three fluids

Gas, propylene, ethylene never mix.

Balances

Flow in equals flow out.

Pressure

Falls everywhere except across a compressor.

Closed loops

Fixed charge; recycles 17 and 24.

Cascade

E-203 links both loops.

A falling receiver level means refrigerant went somewhere else.

Interactive — pick a fluid and a variable

Follow one fluid around the sheet

Rules become visible when one path is traced.

Propylene goes 1.35 → 16.9 → 1.42 bar a — the letdown valve, not the kettle, makes the cold.

Interactive — pick a run, drag the clock

The flags during a disturbance

Red rose, blue fell from the printed value — the sheet is the reference that every change is read against.

The gas train on the PFD and on the P&ID

Same four items, many more marks — the PFD is for the process, the P&ID for the plant.

Interactive — pick a layer

Five things only the P&ID shows

The PFD shows where these sit, not how they act — operating needs both drawings.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Three fluids, two closed loops, one cascade exchanger E-203.
  • Pressure rises only across K-201 and K-301; letdown valves make the cold.
  • In a disturbance the printed flags are the reference.
  • Instruments, fail positions, trips and relief live on the P&ID.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Read each stream by its number, its flag, its source and its destination.

2

Add up the flags before trusting them: mass and heat must balance.

3

Trace one fluid at a time; expect pressure to rise only across a compressor.

4

Open the P&ID for instruments, fail positions, trips and relief.
